run.question: I'm investigating an error in trace TRACE-ERR-X9K2M. Check Elasticsearch and tell me which service failed and what the error was.

report.summary: Elasticsearch answers the question. In index app-245-apm-traces, trace_id "TRACE-ERR-X9K2M" matches exactly two documents, both timestamped 2026-11-21T05:28:00Z. The error-bearing span belongs to service "payment-gateway", operation "authenticate_payment" (span_id span-pay-err, parent_span_id span-gw-err, http.status_code 503, duration_ms 5180), with error.type "ConnectionTimeout" and error.message "Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729"; its stack trace shows payment_gateway/clients/auth_client.py authenticate() awaiting http_client.post(auth_url, json=payload, timeout=5.0) called from process_payment in payment_gateway/handlers/payment_handler.py, and its response body reads "Service Unavailable" / "The payment authentication service is currently unavailable." The other document is service "api-gateway", operation "POST /api/payment" (span_id span-gw-err, no parent reference, 503, 5234 ms) and is the only parent reference in the trace, so the visible edge is api-gateway to payment-gateway. Against the same-index same-operation baseline of 10 TRACE-OK-* traces from 05:14:00Z to 05:23:00Z (245 ms api-gateway POST /api/payment, 180 ms payment-service process_payment, all 200), these two are the only non-200 documents among the 22 the query returned. Observed mechanism: payment-gateway's call to an authentication dependency hit its 5 s client timeout, producing a 503 that was propagated to the api-gateway caller. The authentication dependency itself is not observable in the evidence: no span, document, pod or event identifies it, and Jaeger and Prometheus were unavailable during this Run, so no root object can be named.

claims.text: An exact term query on trace_id "TRACE-ERR-X9K2M" in index app-245-apm-traces returned 2 documents (total 2, none omitted): one at @timestamp 2026-11-21T05:28:00Z for service api-gateway and one at 2026-11-21T05:28:00.050Z for service payment-gateway.
The error-bearing span of TRACE-ERR-X9K2M is service "payment-gateway", operation "authenticate_payment", span_id "span-pay-err", parent_span_id "span-gw-err", http.status_code 503, duration_ms 5180.

That span carries error.type "ConnectionTimeout" and error.message "Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729"; its stack trace names File "/app/payment_gateway/clients/auth_client.py", in authenticate, with response = await self.http_client.post(auth_url, json=payload, timeout=5.0), reached from File "/app/payment_gateway/handlers/payment_handler.py", in process_payment, line 101, result = await self.auth_client.authenticate(payment_method, customer_id, amount). The stack_trace field was cut at 2000 characters.

The http.response.body of the payment-gateway span (cut at 2000 characters) reads "Payment Gateway Error" and "

Service Unavailable

The payment authentication service is currently unavailable.

".

The other span in TRACE-ERR-X9K2M is service "api-gateway", operation "POST /api/payment", span_id "span-gw-err", http.method POST, http.status_code 503, duration_ms 5234, with no parent_span_id field present; the only parent reference in the trace links the payment-gateway span (span-pay-err) to span-gw-err, so the visible edge is api-gateway to payment-gateway.

A same-operation baseline exists in the same index and window: the 22 returned documents (total 22, none omitted) are 10 TRACE-OK-* traces at one-minute intervals from 05:14:00Z to 05:23:00Z where api-gateway "POST /api/payment" is 200 at 245 ms and payment-service "process_payment" is 200 at 180 ms, plus the two TRACE-ERR-X9K2M spans at 05:28:00Z at 5234 ms and 5180 ms with http.status_code 503; those two are the only non-200 documents among the 22.

The distinct service values among those 22 documents are api-gateway, payment-service and payment-gateway; no document belongs to a service whose name contains "auth", so no span, span id or service identity of the authentication dependency named in the error appears in this index for the queried window.

The cluster pod inventory returned 33 pods with none omitted and contains no pod named api-gateway or payment-gateway and no pod whose name contains "auth"; namespace otel-demo holds pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (phase Running, restarts 1, container "payment"). This is object state at query time, not incident-time state.

The only Kubernetes event inside the authorized window is a Warning, reason FailedToCreateEndpoint, involved object kind Endpoints name "loki", event namespace default, first and last timestamp 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z, message "Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints \"loki\" already exists", source endpoint-controller; 15 further events fell outside the window and were dropped before grouping.

Content inconsistency inside the error document: the embedded debug-info timestamps in http.response.body read 2024-01-15T10:15:1Z through 2024-01-15T10:15:11Z while the document @timestamp is 2026-11-21T05:28:00.050Z, and the card number is masked as 4532XXXXXXXX1234 with cvv "***".

The 503 in TRACE-ERR-X9K2M is payment-gateway's client-side timeout of a call to an authentication dependency: error.type ConnectionTimeout, the 5.0 s timeout in auth_client.authenticate and the 5180 ms span duration are consistent with the dependency not answering, and the response body states the payment authentication service is currently unavailable.

Candidates this trace cannot separate: the authentication dependency being down or degraded, versus network or service-discovery failure between payment-gateway and the auth endpoint, versus a misconfigured or too-short timeout in payment-gateway. No span, log line, document or metric for the auth dependency was observed to choose among them.

api-gateway is not the origin of this failure: its span span-gw-err has no parent reference and no error block, and every error detail (error.type ConnectionTimeout, error.message AUTH-4729, the auth_client timeout stack) is recorded on its child span span-pay-err of payment-gateway, so its 503 is the propagated result.

The app-282/loki FailedToCreateEndpoint Warning at 05:28:04Z is not a cause of this trace's 503: the event's own message attributes it to endpoint creation for service app-282/loki, a different application namespace and object from the payment trace, and no event references payment-gateway or api-gateway.

The failing spans' service identities api-gateway and payment-gateway have no matching pods in the pod inventory, while the otel-demo payment pod is named payment (payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d) and the baseline spans in the same index use service "payment-service"; the apm-trace identities therefore cannot be tied to the payment workload by name from this evidence.

Identify and check the authentication endpoint configured in payment_gateway/clients/auth_client.py (auth_url) - its readiness, latency, and its budget against the 5 s client timeout - since the timeout is the immediate mechanism and that service is otherwise unobserved here.

Re-run the trace lookup in Jaeger once reachable and query the authentication dependency's own error and latency signals (for example traces_span_metrics_calls_total by service_name and status_code, and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds on payment-gateway) so the dependency, not just its caller, can be assessed.

gaps: Jaeger could not corroborate the trace: traces_query_trace_by_id for "TRACE-ERR-X9K2M" returned status error with reason INVALID_PARAMS and null content; traces_search (service "payment", 2026-11-21T05:20:00Z-05:30:00Z) and traces_list_services both returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. The Jaeger span graph beyond the two Elasticsearch documents is unknown.

Prometheus was unavailable during this Run: get_label_values on status_code for {__name__=~"traces_span_metrics_calls_total"} and a metrics_range_query of sum by (service_name, span_name, status_code)(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code!="STATUS_CODE_UNSET"}[600s])) over 05:20-05:30 both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so service-level error counts and latency for payment-gateway, api-gateway and any auth dependency are unknown and must not be read as zero.

The authentication dependency named in the error ("Authentication service ... AUTH-4729") has no span, document, pod or event in any source queried, so its identity, namespace, runtime kind and health are unknown; consequently no root object can be named.

The log view fetch_pod_logs on otel-demo pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d with filter error|timeout|auth|fail over 05:20:00Z-05:30:00Z returned status no_data (0 of 42 lines read matched), and it is unknown whether that pod is the same workload as the traced "payment-gateway"; the payment application logs therefore neither confirm nor clear this failure.
error.stack_trace, http.request.body and http.response.body were each cut at 2000 characters, so the omitted remainder of those fields is unknown.

Only documents inside the authorized window were read from app-245-apm-traces; whether the index holds traces outside 2026-11-20T05:30:07Z-2026-11-21T05:30:07Z, or from services not present in the 22 returned documents, is unknown.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so whether any deployment or configuration change preceded the 05:28:00Z failure could not be checked.
next_steps: Locate the auth_url / authentication service used by payment_gateway/clients/auth_client.py and inspect its own error and latency signals around 2026-11-21T05:28:00Z.
Restore Jaeger and Prometheus access, then fetch TRACE-ERR-X9K2M with a valid Jaeger-format trace ID to recover the full span graph.
Confirm the mapping between the apm-trace service names api-gateway/payment-gateway/payment-service and the otel-demo workloads before attributing pod-level evidence to the traced services.
